en: The Apadāna of the Elder Udapānadāyaka Kumuda Chapter 4.4 I gave a well to the Saṅgha, To those who were free from desire. By that merit, through this deed, I was reborn in heaven. For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in the world of the gods. When my lifespan there had ended, I was born here in the human world. In the city of Bhaddiya, I was born into a wealthy family. My name was Udapāna, And I was known as the giver of wells. I gave many thousands of wells To the Saṅgha, which is worthy of offerings. Having given these excellent wells, I attained the fruit of Stream-entry. I have seen the Buddha, the World-Honored One, The Teacher, the one with vision. Having seen him, I took refuge In the Buddha, Dhamma, and Saṅgha. I have attained the fruit of Stream-entry, A state free from perdition. I shall not be reborn in hell, Nor among animals or ghosts. Having abandoned the human plane, I shall go to the realm of the gods. There I shall dwell for a long time, Enjoying the fruits of my merit. This is my final birth; I am now the last of my existences. Having attained the fruit of Arhatship, I am now cooled and liberated. I have paid homage to the Buddha, The Teacher, the one with vision. Having paid homage to the Buddha, I have transcended all suffering. Thus did the Elder Udapānadāyaka speak his own ancient account.
and having given alms-food, I offered it.”
I dedicated it at that time.
That deed which I performed then, ninety-one aeons ago—
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of that well.
the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Udapānadāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Udapānadāyaka is the fourth.
